title: Join A with B and B with A
description:
Given the sets `A = {19, 22, 24, 20, 25, 26}` and `B = {19, 22, 20, 25, 26, 24, 28, 27}`: Join A with B and B with A.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as `union_both_ways(a, b)`, returning a tuple `(sorted list of a joined with b, sorted list of b joined with a)`, showing that joining is the same regardless of which set comes first.
hints: You need to join the sets in each order and return both results together so they can be compared.
Joining two sets uses the same union operation either way - only the order of the arguments to it changes.
expected_behavior: Returns a 2-tuple: the sorted union of a with b, and the sorted union of b with a. Both lists should be equal, since set union does not depend on argument order.
explanation: Set union is commutative - a.union(b) and b.union(a) always contain the same elements, regardless of argument order, because union just combines every element from both sets and collapses duplicates.
